answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
**How long before I can run again, and the Thanksgiving 10K in 5 weeks?**

Give the running legs a full week off first. Walk daily this week, 20–30 minutes, and let the quad soreness and blister fully settle. If everything feels normal by Saturday or Sunday, a slow 2–3 mile shuffle is fine; if not, wait another few days. No shame in two full weeks of walking.

Next week we rebuild gently with short easy miles only, no workouts. By week three you can add a slightly longer easy run.

The Thanksgiving 10K is possible, but only as a fun run, not a race. Five weeks is enough to feel springy again but not enough to recover, rebuild, and sharpen for a hard 10K effort so soon after 26.2. Line up, run it at a comfortable conversational pace, enjoy the day with your friend, and treat any pass as a bonus. Racing it hard risks a setback that costs you the whole winter.

new.analysis:
## Why this week looks like this

The body took a real hit on Sunday: 3h 50m, 63% of time in zone 4, drift from 157 to 164, and a classic "20-mile wall" where the last 10K slowed by about a minute per mile. That is the pattern of glycogen running low and quads overloading on the downhills, not of a fitness problem. The front 20 at 8:30/mi was right on your under-3:45 math.

The real recovery work for the next week or two is sleep, walking, food and the blister healing, not running. Easy jogging too early tends to extend the soreness rather than shorten it. The research-and-practice rule of thumb for a marathon is roughly one easy day per mile raced before you touch anything structured, which lands us in mid-November.

I have not planned past this week on purpose. Tell me what you want to point at next: a spring half or marathon, a faster 10K in the new year, a base-building winter, or just enjoying running without a bib. That answer shapes everything from here, including how seriously to treat the Thanksgiving 10K.

Nice work out there. Twelve minutes off a marathon PR is a big step, and the pacing discipline through 20 miles is what you should take forward into the next build.
